# Micropage

Micropage compiles a line-oriented `.page` file into a static site with working forms.

Site: https://micropage.sh
App: https://app.micropage.sh
Docs: https://docs.micropage.sh
Blog: https://micropage.sh/content
Showcase (live source files): https://micropage.sh/showcase
Markup design notes: https://micropage.sh/content/designing-markup-for-ai-agents

## When to use this

- Landing pages, waitlists, small multi-page marketing sites
- Pages an LLM should generate and later edit without inventing components
- Sites that should remain a text file in git

Do not use this for pixel-perfect marketing sites, app UIs, or design systems. Use Framer, Webflow, or a real frontend stack.

## File shape

One project can contain one or more `.page` files. A typical file:

1. `[site]` block — title, description, logo, colors, lang
2. Optional `[nav]` and `[footer]`
3. One or more page blocks: `[Home -> /]`, `[About -> /about]`
4. Sections inside each page: `/// hero`, `/// section`, optional `/// html`

## Grammar (closed vocabulary)

Emit one element per line. Do not nest tags. Do not invent element names. Do not use inline colors.

Site keys (non-exhaustive): title, description, logo, favicon, lang, keywords, theme_color, og_image, og_type, type, profiles, email, alternate_name, founded, legal_name

Site identity: `type:` is organization (default) or person. `profiles:` takes comma-separated URLs of your accounts elsewhere (schema.org sameAs; an x.com link also sets twitter:site). `founded:` and `legal_name:` are organization only. `twitter_handle:` is no longer supported. Every page's JSON-LD (identity with @id {site url}/#organization or #person, WebSite, BlogPosting on posts) is generated from `[site]`. A page with its own `<script type="application/ld+json">` in a `/// html` block or inline html element gets no generated JSON-LD; footer JSON-LD counts for every page. Hand-written JSON-LD should reuse the platform @id for the identity.

Site colors go in an indented block inside `[site]`: `colors:` then `  primary: #5c6fff` on the next line (also secondary, success, warning, info, danger; hex only). Optional `[site.dark]` takes `colors:` and `logo:` and applies when the visitor's system is in dark mode.

Blog block (optional, for the /content posts archive): `[blog]` then `title:` and `description:` lines. Separate from the site description.

Nav entries: `Label -> /path` or `btn: Label -> url` / `btn-outline: Label -> url`

Page header: `[Name -> /path]`
Optional page meta: `meta:` then indented description, og_type, canonical, keywords, and:
- `lang: ro` (or `pt-BR`) — this page's `<html lang>`; default is the site `lang`, else `en`
- `translation: en -> /about` — repeatable; links a translated version (made reciprocal automatically, emitted as `hreflang`; links to missing pages are ignored)

Languages: put each language in a folder (`[Acasă -> /ro]`, `[Despre -> /ro/despre]`). A language folder sets the page language when its code is used in a `lang:` or `translation:` line, or the folder holds at least two pages (so `/it/services` alone stays in the site language). Nav, footer and /content are shared by all languages.

Sections:
- `/// hero` optional `align:center` `bg:primary|primary-subtle|secondary|muted|success|warning|info|danger|dark|light`
- `/// section` same optional modifiers
- `/// html` — raw HTML; agents should avoid this unless asked

Elements:
- `h1:` `h2:` `h3:` `h4:` `h5:`
- `p:` — the rest of the line is literal text
- `small:`
- `- item` (unordered) / `1. item` (ordered; starts at the first number) — one item per line, consecutive lines form one list; a blank line or switching `-`/`1.` starts a new list; no nesting, plain text; works in sections, columns, footer. Use `p:` for a paragraph starting with `- ` or `2024. `
- `table: Caption` (optional) then `| A | B |` rows — first row is the header; `|---|` separator optional; plain-text cells; `\|` is a literal pipe
- `icon: bi bi-name` (Bootstrap Icons)
- `img: Description <- filename.png` (the words before `<-` become the alt text), `img: alt: text <- filename.png` (explicit, wins if both are present) or `img: <- filename.png` (empty alt)
- `button: Label -> url`
- `btn-secondary: Label -> url`
- `btn-outline: Label -> url`
- `link: Label -> url`
- `link: Label <- file.pdf` or `link: <- file.pdf`
- `col:` starts a column; following indented-looking lines still sit at column scope as sibling element lines until the next `col:` or section
- `form: name`
- `input: Label` or `input: Label*`, optional trailing `type:email|tel|name|organization|text` (`input: Courriel* type:email`; same for `textfield:`)
- `text:` / `textarea:`
- `select: Label [A, B, C]`
- `checkboxes: Label [A, B]`
- `radios: Label [A, B]`
- `submit: Label`
- `success: Message` — confirmation text after a successful submit; optional, max 300 chars
- `newsletter: true` / `newsletter: false`

`*` at the end of a field label means required. With an input `type:`, the `*` can go before or after it.

Autofill: an `input:` with one of these exact labels (any case) gets a hint automatically and stays a text input:
- email, e-mail, email address, e-mail address, your email, your email address, work email: autocomplete email, inputmode email
- name, full name, your name, your full name: autocomplete name
- phone, phone number, telephone, your phone, your phone number: autocomplete tel, inputmode tel
- company, company name, organization, organisation: autocomplete organization

For other labels and languages use the trailing `type:` (after a space, only these values):
- `type:email`: email input and autocomplete email
- `type:tel`: tel input and autocomplete tel
- `type:name`: autocomplete name
- `type:organization`: autocomplete organization
- `type:text`: text input, no hint

Autofill hints are only for the visitor's own details: add `type:text` when a matching field asks about someone or something else (friend, attendee, pet). `type:email` makes the browser block anything that isn't one well-formed address (`john at gmail`, two addresses, `none`); the server doesn't check the format. On a newsletter form keep `email` in the label: subscriber capture ignores `type:email` and doesn't recognize `E-mail` or labels like `Courriel`.

Form confirmation: without `success:`, a form shows `Thank you. Your message was sent.` and a newsletter form shows `Thank you. You're subscribed.` (and no Submit again button). `newsletter:` in markup only chooses the wording — subscriber capture is enabled per form in the web app, never from markup.

Images and file links: `<- filename` resolves a file uploaded to the project (not a URL on `link:`; never combine `<-` and `->` on a link). Do not hardcode random remote URLs unless asked.

## Rules for agents

- Prefer editing the existing `.page` file in place.
- Read PROJECT_AGENT.md in the project if present — it has tokens and tone.
- Keep structure stable across edits. Change copy and order before inventing new sections.
- Do not wrap the file in markdown fences when writing it back.
- Keyboard focus: theme controls, `link:` lines and underlined links in text get the theme's focus ring. Other Bootstrap components in raw HTML (`accordion-button`, `page-link`, `btn-close`, `btn-check`, `form-range`, `form-control-plaintext`, `focus-ring`, carousel controls) can have no outline, so add a `:focus-visible` outline for any you use. Tab and Shift+Tab show the focused element below a header pinned to the top (JavaScript only; not on scroll-snapping pages, on pages that scroll inside `body` or a wrapper, or inside your own sticky or fixed elements; untested in Safari). Focus inside an iframe can land under the header, and so can tabbing out of one. Anchor targets are not moved: if one lands under the header, put `scroll-margin-top` on that target. Don't add `scroll-padding` on `html`: in Chromium it makes the page jump when focus moves into the sticky header.
- Describe every image before `<-`: those words become its alt text. What the generated HTML does for accessibility: https://docs.micropage.sh/docs/concepts/accessibility/
- Do not emit React, Tailwind class soup, or custom components.
- After edits, the human publishes from the web app (Publish) or `micropage publish` (Pro CLI). Agents connected through the Micropage MCP server (`@micropage-sh/mcp`, Pro) save drafts with `save_page` and call `publish_build` only when the user asks: https://docs.micropage.sh/docs/mcp/overview/

## Minimal example

```
[site]
title: Harbor
description: A waitlist

[nav]
Pricing -> /pricing
btn: Join -> /#waitlist

[Home -> /]

/// hero
h1: Launch the waitlist tonight
p: Edit this file. Publish. Collect email.
button: Join the list -> /#waitlist

/// section
form: waitlist
input: Email*
submit: Get early access
```

## Plans (for support answers)

Prices are in USD and exclude VAT/sales tax; Paddle (merchant of record) adds tax for the buyer's country at checkout. Form submission limits are per project, per calendar month (UTC); spam-flagged submissions don't count.

- Free: 1 project, starter AI credits, 100 submissions per project per month, `*.micropage.live` host, badge
- Pro ($6/mo or $49/yr): custom domain, newsletter sending (optionally from your own sending domain), CLI, MCP server, zip export, CSV, daily submission digest, no badge, 5 projects, 1,000 submissions per project per month
- Pro+ ($12/mo or $98/yr): everything in Pro, plus webhooks, instant email per submission, CI deploy tokens, priority builds, 20 projects, 10,000 submissions per project per month
